summary: Quickstart RAG template: streaming responses disconnect behind corporate proxy (SSE/HTTP chunked closed mid-generation)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports frequent streaming disconnects (SSE) when running the RAG+agent quickstart template behind a corporate proxy. The request succeeds for non-streaming mode, but streaming often terminates mid-generation with client-side network errors.

Impact:
- End-user chat UI hangs or returns partial output.
- Retries sometimes re-run tool calls, increasing token cost and producing inconsistent responses.
- Blocks customer from deploying template to internal network without disabling proxy.

Customer context:
DevFoundry is evaluating Redwood hosted API using the TypeScript RAG+agent template. They are routing outbound traffic through a corporate proxy (Zscaler-like). They see failures primarily on longer responses (>30–60s) and during bursts.

Environment:
- Redwood Hosted API (prod), region us-east
- Template: TypeScript RAG+agent quickstart (internal beta)
- Runtime: Node 20
- Deployment: internal k8s behind corporate egress proxy (HTTP CONNECT)
- Proxy behaviors suspected: response buffering, idle timeout, HTTP/2 translation

What we think is happening:
- Proxy closes long-lived HTTP connections or buffers event-stream responses and terminates early.
- Some proxies drop chunked responses if they don’t see bytes within an idle window, or if they can’t classify Content-Type: text/event-stream.
- Client currently treats disconnect as generic fetch/network error; template doesn’t always attempt safe streaming resume.

Requested outcome:
- Guidance + safe defaults for running streaming behind proxies (timeouts/keepalive, proxy buffering settings, fall back to non-streaming).
- Template mitigation to handle disconnects gracefully (detect partial generation, retry with idempotency guidance, tool-call safety).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Deploy the TypeScript RAG+agent quickstart template in an environment where outbound HTTPS goes through a corporate proxy (CONNECT).
2) Enable streaming in the template UI/API route.
3) Ask a question that produces a long answer (e.g., request a multi-section report) and triggers retrieval + at least one tool call.
4) Observe that the streaming response ends mid-token with client error. Subsequent retry may produce different answer and may re-run tool calls.

Notes:
- Disconnections are more frequent when response time > ~45s.
- Non-streaming requests to the same endpoint typically succeed.
expected_result: Streaming response completes successfully; client receives final event and can render full assistant message. If network disconnect occurs, template should surface a user-actionable error and avoid unsafe automatic retries that can re-run tools unexpectedly.
actual_result: Streaming response terminates early. Client throws network error and the server route logs show aborted upstream connection. In some cases, the proxy returns 200 but closes the tunnel during the stream.
customer_logs:
Customer-provided client error (browser console):
- TypeError: fetch failed
- cause: ECONNRESET

Customer-provided server logs (Node):
2025-03-06T19:22:14.773Z error request_id=rwreq_01HSJ7ZK8G8K3Y9F3C3B7F4A1A msg="stream interrupted" err="AbortError: The operation was aborted"
2025-03-06T19:22:14.774Z info  request_id=rwreq_01HSJ7ZK8G8K3Y9F3C3B7F4A1A msg="upstream closed during SSE" upstream="https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/chat/completions"

Proxy snippet (from customer network team, sanitized):
TLS tunnel established -> idle timeout 60s policy; connection closed by policy when downstream read stalled

HTTP headers observed:
Content-Type: text/event-stream
Transfer-Encoding: chunked
redwood_investigation_notes:
Support triage:
- Verified customer API key is valid; not seeing 401/429 patterns.
- Redwood gateway logs show normal 200 stream start, followed by client disconnect (499-equivalent) before final token.
- No correlated 5xx spikes in us-east for the timeframe.

Hypotheses checked:
1) Redwood server-side timeout: Not indicated; gateway stream timeout is higher than reported durations; other customers streaming fine.
2) Client-side timeout: Node fetch default doesn’t time out, but intermediaries may.
3) Proxy buffering/idle timeout: Matches symptoms; disconnect around ~60s aligns with policy.

Data points:
- In our logs, request_id examples from customer show FIN/RST from client side mid-stream.
- When customer disabled proxy for a test pod, disconnects stopped.

Conclusion:
This is primarily an intermediary/proxy compatibility issue with long-lived SSE streams. We need clear docs + template defaults (keepalive, flush bytes, and controlled fallback to non-streaming).
mitigation_workaround:
Workarounds provided to customer:
1) Proxy config (preferred):
- Disable response buffering for Content-Type: text/event-stream
- Increase idle timeout for CONNECT tunnels and downstream reads (recommend >= 5 minutes)
- Ensure HTTP/1.1 streaming is supported end-to-end (avoid HTTP/2 translation if it buffers)

2) App/template config:
- Add periodic SSE comment/heartbeat bytes (e.g., ": ping\n\n" every 10–15s) to keep the connection active through proxies.
- If using an ingress (nginx), set:
  - proxy_buffering off;
  - proxy_read_timeout 300s;
  - proxy_send_timeout 300s;
  - chunked_transfer_encoding on;
- Provide a user-facing toggle to disable streaming and use non-streaming responses in constrained network environments.

3) Retry guidance:
- Do NOT automatically retry tool-calling turns on disconnect without guardrails.
- If retrying, retry only non-tool steps or require user confirmation; log a single error event with correlation ID.

Customer confirmed proxy team can try increasing idle timeouts and disabling buffering for SSE routes.
resolution:
Resolved with documented mitigation + template changes queued:
- Support provided proxy + ingress configuration guidance for SSE streaming and suggested a streaming heartbeat to avoid idle timeouts.
- Engineering aligned to update templates to:
  (a) emit periodic SSE heartbeat comments during long generations,
  (b) improve error messaging when streams terminate mid-response,
  (c) add a documented fallback to non-streaming mode for proxy-restricted environments.

Customer outcome:
Customer confirmed that increasing proxy idle timeout and disabling buffering reduced disconnects significantly in staging. They will keep streaming enabled for external users and provide non-streaming fallback for internal users until template update lands.

Follow-ups:
- Track template update in quickstarts repo and update troubleshooting docs to include 'Streaming behind proxies' section.
- Consider SDK-level guidance/error typing improvements (TS SDK streaming reconnect work already in progress).
